title: Check yourself: Pinning model ids and migrating safely

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team changes one configuration value from an older id to Claude Opus 5.5 and every call starts failing with 400. Their call sets a manual thinking budget. Which fix does the page back?

options.text: Drop the settings that the new target rejects, and build per target
options.says: The page says an item that is "rejected" returns a 400 error and that the guide lists what to remove: a manual `budget_tokens` is rejected on Opus 5.5.

options.text: Raise `max_tokens`, since a budget needs more room under the new id
options.says: Ruled out because "Sending thinking of type disabled, or a manual budget_tokens, is rejected", whatever the room.

options.text: Add retries, since a 400 on a fresh deployment is often transient
options.says: Ruled out because a rejected setting fails every time, and a rising 400 rate is "the signal of a rejected parameter".

options.text: Keep the old id and pin the new one on a second key
options.says: Ruled out because the page says to make the request builder per model and "Change the request builder together with the id".

questions.stem: A deprecated id is still called by a nightly job that nobody remembers. How does the page say to find it?

options.text: Export the Console usage as a CSV and read it by key and model
options.says: The page says "usage broken down by API key and model" shows which key still calls which model.

options.text: Wait for the retirement email, which names each calling application
options.says: Ruled out because the notice is about dates, "providing at least 60 days' notice before model retirement for publicly released models", and names no callers.

options.text: Ask the model for its own version in a test prompt
options.says: Ruled out because the page's own method is the export that shows "usage broken down by API key and model", while a prompt returns text and no record of calls.

options.text: Check the alias list, which names every application that resolves it
options.says: Ruled out because an alias is "a convenience pointer that resolves to the dated ID" and holds no list of callers.

questions.stem: The same team runs on the Claude API and on a cloud service. One model has a published retirement day. What does the page say about the same model there?

options.text: It stops sixty days earlier, to give notice to its customers
options.says: Ruled out because the only fixed period on the page is "at least 60 days' notice", counted before retirement on the operator's own schedule.

options.text: It stops on the same date, because the model id is identical
options.says: Ruled out because the dates listed apply to "the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS and Microsoft Foundry".

options.text: The partner that operates it sets its own schedule
options.says: The page says "Partner-operated platforms (Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud) set their own retirement schedules".

options.text: It becomes an alias of the replacement on the date
options.says: Ruled out because the page names no aliasing on retirement: "Requests to retired models will fail."
